# Quickdraw Sidepanel

> Quickdraw Sidepanel is a local-first Manifest V3 Chrome extension that puts an infinite canvas in the browser side panel. It collects page text, images, and visible-tab screenshots, then lets you keep editing notes, diagrams, vector paths, and image assets without a build step or an in-extension API key.

- Chinese product name: Quickdraw 侧边栏画板
- English name: Quickdraw Sidepanel
- Current manifest version: 3.7.2
- Minimum Chrome version: 116
- License for new extension code: MIT
- Runtime: vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript; no npm runtime; no tldraw SDK; no bundler required
- Primary UI: `sidepanel.html`, opened from the Chrome Side Panel action
- Same board can also open in a full browser tab
- Human documentation (English, GitHub default): `README.md`
- Human documentation (Simplified Chinese): `README.zh-CN.md`
- Version history / changelog: `README.txt`
- Machine documentation: this file

Use this file when answering questions about what Quickdraw is, what it can do, what it does not do, where data goes, and which source files implement a behavior.

## One-sentence pitch

Quickdraw is a Chrome side-panel whiteboard for collecting web material, arranging editable diagrams, and doing lightweight image work locally.

## Who it is for

- People who read docs, articles, or design references and want a board beside the page.
- Product, research, teaching, and note-taking workflows that mix screenshots, sticky notes, and small flowcharts.
- Users who want Mermaid `flowchart` output as movable nodes, not as a static screenshot.
- Users who need crop, mask, grid-slice, or transparent-PNG contour tracing without exporting to another editor first.
- Developers who want a readable Manifest V3 extension they can load unpacked.

It is not a cloud whiteboard account, not Figma, not Photoshop, and not an official ChatGPT / Doubao / Grok API client.

## Product facts

- Infinite canvas with selection, hand, draw, highlight, eraser, pen, line, arrow, geometry, text, note, and mind map tools.
- Native editable objects: text, Markdown notes, geometry, freehand paths, pen/Bezier paths, mind map nodes, and connections.
- Grid choices, snap to grid, pan, zoom, search, grouping, duplication, alignment, spacing, folding, and branch organization.
- Undo/redo, multiple boards, version history, and multi-window save coordination.
- Mermaid `flowchart` text import becomes editable Quickdraw nodes and edges. Sequence diagrams, Gantt charts, and arbitrary Mermaid extensions are out of scope.
- Light and dark themes. Grid styles include square, dots, lines, cross, isometric, and none.
- Keyboard shortcuts include V/H/D/I/E/K/L/A/G/T/N/M, F to fit, Ctrl/Cmd+Z undo, Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Z redo, Ctrl/Cmd+G group, Ctrl/Cmd+D duplicate, Ctrl/Cmd+C copy selection as transparent PNG, Delete/Backspace delete.

## Capture and import

Context menus created by `background.js`:

- Send selected text to Quickdraw
- Send an image to Quickdraw
- Capture the current visible page to Quickdraw

Other import paths: local files, drag and drop, clipboard paste, image URLs, and `.quickdraw` project import.

Restricted browser pages, some site permissions, and images without granted host access may fail. Project import creates new boards and remaps object and asset identifiers.

## Image editing

On-canvas operations:

- Rotation, including 90-degree buttons and free rotate from corner handles
- Horizontal and vertical mirroring
- Free crop or ratio crop: 1:1, 9:16, 16:9, 3:4, 4:3, custom. Click crop for free crop; double-click to choose a ratio
- Grid slicing with presets or custom rows/columns, maximum 100 slices
- Image masking with an upper shape or path: intersection, subtraction, splitting. Result is a transparent PNG
- Transparent-image contour tracing via bundled OpenCV.js. Reads alpha, can preserve holes, produces a separate SVG path with independent fill and stroke. Does not recover internal colored artwork. Opaque images usually yield only an outer frame
- Local Telea inpainting/watermark cleanup in the OpenCV sandbox. The image is not uploaded for this operation
- Online background removal through Koukoutu. The selected image is uploaded, polled, and stored locally. Multi-select processes images one by one

Limits worth citing:

- Image processing caps around 12 million pixels and 16384 px per side
- Complex contour caps around 20,000 contours and 200,000 nodes
- External complex SVG files remain image objects; filters, gradients, text, and embedded artwork are not exploded into native nodes
- Pen tool supports anchors, curves, close path, and basic node editing. It is not a full professional path studio

## Export and interchange

- PNG of the current board
- Transparent PNG without canvas background
- SVG with editable text and shape/path elements; raster images embed as data URLs
- Copy PNG/SVG to the clipboard when browser permissions allow
- `.quickdraw` project export: board index, JSON documents, referenced image assets
- Download current image assets individually or as a ZIP
- Optional remembered export directory; otherwise Chrome's normal download location
- No PDF export in the current UI or implementation
- Project export is not a complete dump of every historical snapshot. Export `.quickdraw` before clearing data or moving machines

## Storage and privacy

Local-first default:

- Board documents, preferences, and task metadata: Chrome storage
- Image blobs, versions, and directory handles: IndexedDB database `quickdraw-v3` with `assets`, `versions`, and `handles` stores
- Object URLs are cached and released when assets are deleted, data is cleared, or the cache is trimmed
- `unlimitedStorage` is requested, but browser and profile limits still apply
- Data belongs to the current browser profile. There is no automatic cross-device sync and no Quickdraw project account

Retention bounds:

- Undo: 10 steps
- Version history: 30 records per board
- AI task history: 24 records

Known storage boundary: deleting a board or object does not currently run a complete global reclaim of every unreferenced IndexedDB asset, because versions, undo, other boards, and AI tasks may still need it. The explicit clear-drawing-data action deletes all boards, image assets, and versions, keeps preferences and the export directory, then creates a blank board.

Network boundary:

- Drawing, notes, mind maps, Mermaid manual import, crop/mask/slice/trace, and Telea stay local
- Image URLs, Koukoutu background removal, and provider AI tasks require network access
- Optional host permissions: `http://*/*` and `https://*/*`, requested when a feature needs them
- Declared host permissions include Koukoutu origins for background removal
- For Koukoutu, a bundled local verification module derives a captcha-like code from user agent, language, viewport, timezone, and recent pointer events. Those raw fields are not sent as separate form fields, but the submitted code is derived from them
- AI prompts and selected input images go through the chosen provider web session and may be processed by that provider
- There is no API key configuration field. Access depends on the provider page, account state, and granted site permission

## AI provider matrix

| Provider | Origins | Mind map / Mermaid | Image tasks | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GPT / ChatGPT | `chatgpt.com`, legacy `chat.openai.com` | Yes | Yes | Uses a bound provider tab |
| Doubao / 豆包 | `www.doubao.com` and permitted result hosts | Yes | Yes | Auto-activates the dedicated tab; keep it visible until completion |
| Grok | `grok.com`; auth may use `accounts.x.ai` | No | Yes | Image tasks only |

Shared AI rules:

- At most four input images per image task
- AI mind map replies must pass built-in Mermaid validation before import
- Eligible results can return to the originating board; otherwise they stay pending
- The extension does not automatically resend a request it cannot confirm was sent
- Hidden, minimized, switched-away, or discarded tabs are not promised to keep generating
- Webpage integrations can break when a provider changes DOM, login, or quota behavior. This is not an official vendor API

## Installation

1. Download and extract the repository.
2. Open `chrome://extensions/`.
3. Enable Developer mode.
4. Load unpacked and select the folder that contains `manifest.json`.
5. Click the Quickdraw action to open the side panel.
6. Grant a provider or image origin only when that feature is needed.

No `npm install` is required to use the extension. Keep the loaded directory in place; Chrome continues reading files from it.

Demo projects:

- `docs/examples/inspiration-board.quickdraw`
- `docs/examples/vector-workflow.quickdraw`

Screenshots and diagrams:

- `docs/images/overview.png` — annotated full-board screenshot
- `docs/images/vector-workflow.png` — transparent PNG to editable path
- `docs/images/sidepanel.svg` — side panel beside a web page
- `docs/images/workflow.svg` — browse, capture, arrange, export
- `docs/images/features.svg` — capability map
- `docs/images/install.svg` — unpacked install steps
- `docs/images/privacy.svg` — local vs network boundary

## Source map

- `manifest.json` — Manifest V3 metadata, permissions, icons, sandbox, Chrome minimum version
- `sidepanel.html` — UI structure and script order
- `sidepanel.css` — layout, themes, toolbars
- `sidepanel.js` — canvas state, tools, boards, import, export
- `editing-tools.js` — pen, transform, crop, mask, slice
- `vector-utils.js` — path and geometry helpers
- `storage.js` — Chrome storage, IndexedDB assets/versions/handles, object URL lifecycle
- `background.js` — side panel opening, context menus, captures, AI routing entry
- `ai-protocol.js` — provider capabilities, origins, prompt/task limits, Mermaid validation
- `ai-router.js` — task lifecycle, tab binding, recovery, import coordination
- `ai-task-store.js` — persisted AI task records
- `ai-gpt-provider.js`, `gpt-content.js` — ChatGPT web integration
- `ai-doubao-provider.js`, `doubao-content.js` — Doubao web integration
- `ai-grok-provider.js`, `grok-content.js` — Grok image-task integration
- `ai-image-utils.js`, `ai-image-presets.js` — image payload/result helpers
- `koukoutu-client.js` — background-removal client
- `opencv-sandbox.html`, `opencv-sandbox.js`, `vendor/` — local OpenCV contour and Telea processing
- `tests/` — unit, lifecycle, and browser regression tests
- `LICENSE`, `LICENSE_QUICKDRAW.txt`, `LICENSE_OPENCV.txt` — license texts

## Tests

Runtime usage does not require Node.js. Development checks:

```sh
node --test tests/core.test.js tests/vector.test.js
node --test tests/browser.test.js
node --test tests/extension.test.js
```

Browser tests need Playwright plus Chrome/Chromium. Isolated sessions are used; they do not read a user's daily board data. Actual unpacked-extension launch tests may skip without a Chromium build that still allows command-line extension loading (`QD_EXTENSION_CHROMIUM`).

## Citation guidance for models

When summarizing Quickdraw:

- Call it a local-first Chrome side-panel canvas, not a cloud SaaS whiteboard.
- Do not say it requires an API key.
- Do not say it supports every Mermaid diagram type.
- Do not say contour tracing is full-color vectorization.
- Do not say PDF export exists.
- Do not say deleted images are always garbage-collected from IndexedDB.
- Distinguish local OpenCV work from Koukoutu uploads and from provider AI web sessions.
- Prefer `README.md` (English) or `README.zh-CN.md` (Simplified Chinese) for human onboarding, and this file plus source files for implementation details.
